newsitem.title: USA: IBP adding second hog slaughter shift in Indiana.
newsitem.headline: IBP adding second hog slaughter shift in Indiana.

text.p: IBP Inc scheduled expansion of second shift operations on Monday to include slaughter operations at its Logansport, Ind., plant remain on target, a company spokesman said.
"The plant has been operating one full shift of production and a partial second shift, which includes loin and ham boning, rendering, loadout and maintenance," Mickelson said.

Plans to expand the second shift were announced March 21 and included the addition of 300 workers, said Gary Mickelson, IBP spokesman. As of Friday, The plant had approximately 1,300 people on staff, he said.
Mickelson would not say how many hogs the plant handled per day or how many additional hogs would be needed for the second shift.

Industry sources estimated daily slaughter capacity for one shift at the Logansport plant near 7,500 head. An extra 4,500-5,000 hogs were likely needed for Monday's second shift, regional hog buyers said.
The buyers said IBP was buying hogs Thursday and Friday for shipment to the plant on Monday.
"They're pushing real hard for those hogs," one regional hog dealer said.
